title: Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy in the treatment of Ovarian Cancer relapse
official: CHIPOR : Randomized phase III study evaluating hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy in the treatment of ovarian cancer relapse
summary: Main objective: To improve overall survival at 12 months for patients in arm with HIPEC compared with patients in arm without HIPEC.
conditions: Ovarian epithelial cancer : intraperitoneal resectable relapse
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patient age ≥ 18 years,
2. Hematological functions : PNN > ou = 1.5x109/L, platelets > ou = 100x109/L,
3. No contraindication to general anesthesia for heavy surgery
4. Patient must be informed and the Informed Consent Form signed before any study-specific procedures start.
5. Medical/Public Health insurance coverage
6. Women of child-bearing age must use appropriate contraception during treatment and for 6 months after the end of treatment.
7. Performance Status WHO < 2,
8. Previous treatment for epithelial ovarian cancer, tubal peritoneal primitive
9. Patient with intraperitoneal relapse (more than 6 months after the end of the initial treatment), resectable without distant metastasis (with the exception of communicating pleura effusion, sensitive to platine-based second line chemotherapy and resectable lymph-nodes in the groin or retro peritoneal)
10. Second-line platinum-based pre-operatory chemotherapy: carboplatin-paclitaxel or carboplatin-caelix (pegylated liposomal doxorubicine: with gemcitabine, trabectidine, hycamtin authorized)
11. Complete cytoreductive surgery,
12. Delay between the last cycle of second-line chemotherapy and surgery must be between 5 and 12 weeks
13. No hepatic insufficiency (bilirubin ≤ 1.5 the Upper Limit of Normal (ULN), ASAT and ALAT ≤ 3 ULN,
14. No renal insufficiency (creatinine ≤ 1.5 ULN, creatinine clearance >60 ml/min) calculated with MDRD method,
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patient age <18 years,
2. Non-epithelial ovarian tumor,
3. Uncontrolled infection,
4. Patient unwilling or in the incapacity to comply with the medical follow-up required by the trial because of geographic, social or psychological reasons.
5. Clinically significant cardiorespiratory disease contraindicating the hyper hydration required for HIPEC,
6. Patient who has already been treated by HIPEC for ovarian cancer,
7. Persons kept in detention, or incapable of giving consent, or without a Public Health insurance coverage,
8. Pregnant or breastfeeding woman
9. Patient who has already been enrolled in another clinical trial
10. Previous cancer in the last 5 years (except cutaneous baso-cellular epithelioma or uterine peripheral epithelioma),
11. Known hypersensitivity to cisplatin,
12. Metastasis,
13. Use of anti-angiogenic treatment within 8 weeks before surgery
14. Patient with other concomitant severe life threatening disease,
15. More than 2 segmental resections concomitant to HIPEC is foreseen,
16. Any progressive disease during the second-line chemotherapy (platine-based),
17. Relapse occurring less than 6 months after the end of the initial treatment,
